You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

The test `testCompressedHeaderWithNonDefaultDictionarySize()` in class `SevenZFileTest` of the `SevenZFile` component is failing. The test attempts to create a `SevenZFile` object by opening a 7z file, but it fails with a 16 MB dictionary size.

Looking at the current bug report, the user encountered an exception when trying to open a 7z file with a 16 MB dictionary size using this component.

By examining the code snippets, we can see that the `SevenZFile` constructor is invoked with a file obtained through the `getFile` method from `AbstractTestCase`. The `getFile` method loads a file from the classpath based on the provided path.

The failure in the test case indicates that the issue may be related to the handling of dictionary sizes in the `SevenZFile` component, possibly when processing the 7z file with a 16 MB dictionary size. Further investigation into how the `SevenZFile` component handles dictionary sizes and opening 7z files with specific configurations may help in identifying the root cause of the failure.

Do you have any specific methods in mind that you would like to inspect further to diagnose the issue?

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
